answer: Day after day the broad weaver twists the selvedge cords tight with the fingers, rolling the cords tight between the palms. Warp madder reed maker silk bond carries the twisting: a bond madder reed makers lodge after reed bench trials. The delta tends the selvedge, the kernel tends the twisting, the beacon tends the cords. A counterfeit needs 281 false selvedges and 281 false twistings.
